case.description: laminar mixed convection, vertical pipe, buoyancy-assisting, constant wall heat flux

truth_independence.open_issue: prior implementation marked this substrate divergent_truth_substrate=False; unresolved

stage_1.covers: sections 1-8 and the result vocabulary in section 9

stage_2.covers: the corroboration criterion and its equivalence margin
stage_2.form: a decision RULE over the class balance, not a number chosen against it. The rule is specified before the balance is seen and evaluated after.
stage_2.must_be_locked_before: labels, flags and class balance are computed

must_record: measurement sources: publication, table or figure, digitisation method
available operating points with their (Re, Gr*)
eligibility under the section 1 evaluable rule, with a reason per point
whether each eligible point carries a stated uncertainty, and its source
the redistribution determination for each source
must_not_record: trustworthy / untrustworthy labels or their counts
class balance, or any count derived from comparing predictions against truth
measurement_inventory.why: labels and flags are OUTCOMES: the label rule applied to predictions, truth and uncertainty, and the flag rule applied to calibration and materiality. Seeing them before the stage-2 lock means choosing the criterion knowing which way it falls.

result_vocabulary.reproduced_means: a close rerun of the original evaluation: same grid, same truth source, same counterfactual
result_vocabulary.reproduced_unreachable_because: the original inputs are gone; this reconstruction necessarily changes the grid, the truth source and the counterfactual
result_vocabulary.matching_result_is_called: independent corroboration of the causal finding
result_vocabulary.rejected_test: containment of the original value in the reconstruction's confidence interval. A value inside an interval is a failure to reject, not a demonstration of agreement; a wide enough interval contains almost anything. Equivalence requires a margin and a test against it, and the margin cannot be chosen before the measurements are known.
result_vocabulary.removed_proposals: min evaluable points = 12 and max interval width = 0.35, both withdrawn as numbers picked in ignorance of the data

outcomes.CORROBORATED: independently supports the causal finding under the stage-2 criterion
outcomes.INCONCLUSIVE: available measurements cannot support a metric claim either way

invariants: metrics are always reported with their uncertainty, never as bare point estimates
the numbers presented are the reconstruction's; the original triple is never presented as a number this repository produces
result_vocabulary.consistent_with: known-results-declaration.md; neither may change without the other

original_construction.surrogate: forced-convection closure Nu_forced(Re) fitted to the gravity-off CFD; implementing code did not survive
original_construction.truth: Mohammed & Salman assisting-flow correlation Eq 13, evaluated densely

shared_input_coupling.relation: E = d - m(1+d) + eps, with E the relative surrogate error and m the materiality
shared_input_coupling.effect: for small d and eps the label rule |E| > tol approaches the flag condition m >= theta; with theta ~= tol a flagged point is labelled untrustworthy
shared_input_coupling.status: mechanism established; NOT established as an identity
conditional_on: step 4 error scale: UNKNOWN (scale is an undefined symbol in the surviving design)
surrogate fit residual eps: UNRECOVERABLE (no coefficients, R2 or residual survive)
sign of d across the grid: NOT ESTABLISHED (two observations, both Ri >= 1.8)
shared_input_coupling.false_positives_remain_possible_when: eps is positive and large enough to offset d - m(1+d); >= +3.3% just above theta under the observed d, rising past +20% at m = 0.26
shared_input_coupling.inversion: recovering precision ~= 1.00 in the reconstruction would be evidence the coupling survived, not evidence the method works

original_construction.grid_bounds_source: https://pure.kfupm.edu.sa/en/publications/heat-transfer-measurements-of-mixed-convection-for-upward-and-dow/ -- Re 400-1600, Gr 1.1e5-7.4e6; matches the step-4 grid. An earlier overrun claim was withdrawn: it used the companion ECM paper's ranges by mistake
original_construction.envelope_vs_coverage: grid bounds lying inside the experimental range does NOT establish measurement coverage at grid points; the evaluable rule must address coverage

source_paper.citation: Mohammed, H. A. & Salman, Y. K. (2008). Experimental Heat Transfer 21(1):1-23
source_paper.test_run_coverage: 4 entrance lengths (L/D 20/40/60/80) x upward and downward

measurement_uncertainty.note: single global maximum; no per-condition band is reported

source_paper.CORRECTION: the +/-8% figure this project carried as experimental uncertainty is the scatter of the data about the fitted correlation (paper: 'the overall accuracy of heat transfer data in these correlations ... of the order of +/-8%, as shown in Figure 16'). The MEASUREMENT uncertainty on Nu is +/-1.27%. Do not use 8% as measurement uncertainty.

individual_values.figure_16: Log Nu vs Log Ra/Re, Re 400-1600, Gr 1.1e5-7.4e6 -- the average-Nu data the correlation was fitted through
individual_values.recovery_method: exact extraction of marker coordinates from the PDF content stream; axis calibration is the only error source. NOT visual digitisation.

source_paper.label_rule_entanglement: truth choice determines which uncertainty enters the label rule: 1.27% for a measured value, 8% for a correlation. A THIRD term, plot-extraction error, is not yet quantified and could dominate. NO claim is made about whether the second condition binds.

extraction.earlier_extraction_was_wrong: a first pass reported 40 markers in two classes of 20 and guessed they were upward and downward. They were the Sieder & Tate triangles and Brown & Gauvin circles. The present-work markers sit in a second coordinate space at 4.1677x scale that the first pass discarded.
extraction.recorded_ambiguity: the paper states 88 runs over 4 entrance lengths and both directions (~44 upward). 63 distinct upward markers does not reconcile with 44, and the caption calls the figure 'a sample one of these correlations'. Entrance length per point is UNKNOWN.
extraction.redistribution_determination: NOT MADE; extraction held outside the repository

marker_count.why: the path count overcounts (markers drawn more than once; no threshold reconciles it) and the visual count undercounts (overlapped stars read as one blob). Distinct plotted measurements lie somewhere between ~23 and 81.
marker_count.EARLIER_FIGURE_WITHDRAWN: 63 was reported as the count; it is one clustering threshold's answer, not the count

why: Figure 16's x is a RATIO: a correct Ra/Re does not determine Re and Gr separately -- many (Re, Gr) pairs share one ratio
entrance length L/D is not recoverable per point; the figure aggregates four
without (Re, Gr, L/D) a point cannot be matched to a CFD condition
evaluable_cases.note: a marker count, however accurate, is not a case count

dependency_on_cfd.chain: measured points -> Eq 13 -> CFD accepted (and revised) against Eq 13 -> g-off CFD = Nu_F -> surrogate fitted to Nu_F
dependency_on_cfd.acceptance_criterion: agreement with Eq 13, to within the correlation's own +/-8% band
dependency_on_cfd.consequence: scoring that surrogate against these points is a CONSISTENCY CHECK, not an independent validation, unless the acceptance criterion is changed to one that does not reference Eq 13
dependency_on_cfd.precision_note: the step-3 Nusselt-extraction change is recorded as fixing a physical breakdown under outlet recirculation, not as a response to disagreement with Eq 13; which drove it is not separately recorded

correlation_discrepancy.status: UNRESOLVED -- the figure's axis, the plotted-data mapping, or the presentation of the correlation. At least one is inconsistent with the others. NO explanation is chosen; evidence does not select one.
correlation_discrepancy.WITHDRAWN_INFERENCE: an earlier entry inferred the CFD may have used a wrong Eq-13 argument and that its agreement could be coincidental. WITHDRAWN -- not supported. It compared against the figure's printed axis rather than against the physics, and the axis is itself the thing in question.

cfd_arguments_are_plausible.derivation: Ra/Re = Ri*Re*Pr; the CFD's own Re, Gr and Pr do NOT survive, only Ri, so these are derived by inversion, not recomputed from inputs
cfd_arguments_are_plausible.caveat: this does NOT prove Eq 13 or the CFD is correct; it only removes the wrong-argument inference

what_remains_unresolved.x_values: figure axis reads 1e6-1e8; physically available Ra/Re is 50-13,000
what_remains_unresolved.slope: plotted upward line rises ~3.5% across the figure; Eq 13 would rise ~75%
what_remains_unresolved.rescaling_ruled_out: a constant axis rescaling shifts x without changing slope. Implied exponent is 0.0063 on the physical range versus Eq 13's 0.11868

source_paper.standing_limitation: the CFD was compared with a FITTED CORRELATION, not with measured points. Unchanged by any measurement question above.
